messages:
Indra: kicked off a targeted nightly for kv-cache sharding on 8xA100 (tp=4 pp=2) with the kernel-selector roll-forward. seeing an unexpected tail bump on long-seq (P95 ~17ms vs baseline 13ms). quick notes attached.
perf-bot: nightly://profiles/1930001122 flamegraph + heatmap uploaded. delta: compute -10%, comm +40% -> net +30% token tail.
Rui: was kernel-selector global? or did we only change attention tiling thresholds?
Indra: global flag MODEL_KERNEL_SEL=auto, FUSED_ATTENTION=on. suspect different attention kernels used across ranks for seq>512.
Marta: TP sharding changes inter-GPU KV access pattern. small per-token all-reduces exploded — nvprof shows many tiny messages.
Samir: paste nvprof: sizes and counts? small messages kill NCCL efficiency.
Indra: nvprof snippet:
```
AllReduce: 512B x 7.2k calls -> ~22% time
AttentionKernel: 1.1ms avg
KV-serial: 0.25ms
Comm wait spikes near token boundaries (512/1024)
```
Marta: yep, TP interleaving stripes KV and causes cross-group reductions every step. DP or full replicate avoids those comms.
Rui: but DP replication multiplies mem cost and hurts large models. tradeoffs.
Samir: mitigation ideas: 1) TP-local kv placement (keep shard local to TP group), 2) hot-key replication for top-1% keys, 3) NCCL fusion / coalescing, 4) kernel-selector sync across ranks.
Indra: tried tp_local quickly: P95 improved ~9% vs rolled baseline, but per-GPU util skewed badly for real-time burst traces.
perf-bot: skew per-gpu util: [82,39,78,36,80,35,85,33] -> heavy imbalance.
Marta: hybrid: make most keys local (tp_local) + replicate a small hot-key set. reduces comm while limiting hotspot risk.
Rui: we also observed compute latency drop after kernel change, so comm became exposed. kernel-selector now hides compute variability differently across ranks.
Samir: propose to broadcast chosen kernel path each step (KERNEL_SYNC=true) so all ranks pick same fast path and overlap predictably.
Indra: added a repro tool: ./tools/kv_shard_bench --model 40B --tp 4 --pp 2 --seq 1024 --mode realtime. logs attached.
Rui: another lever: adaptive batching — expand fuse window when inter-arrival stable; shrink for low-latency interactive. tested static increase (8ms->14ms) reduced P95 but added cold-start ~18ms.
Marta: adaptive seems promising. also add microbench measuring all-reduce cost vs message size to auto-tune NCCL fuse thresholds.
Samir: experiment plan:
- tp_local + hot-key replicate PoC
- kernel-selector broadcast (KERNEL_SYNC=true)
- run NCCL-fuse microbench to find optimal fuse window per hw
- adaptive batching prototype wired to token-interarrival telemetry
Marta: I'll take hot-key replication PoC and heatmap telemetry (1s buckets, per-key counters).
Rui: I'll land kernel broadcast and run microbench. Indra can run the tp_local baseline matrix.
Indra: will also try rolling back attention-tiling patch (commit 9f4a679) behind ATTENTION_TILE_V2=false to check regression path.
perf-bot: regression-tracker flagged commit 9f4a679 -> +11% P95 on nightlies.
Samir: also test non-uniform kernel thresholds as a variable; sync should reduce compute skew and improve overlap.
Marta: TL;DR: root cause = comm exposed by compute speedups + TP kv striping producing many tiny all-reduces. mitigations: tp_local + hot-key replication, kernel sync, adaptive batching, NCCL fuse auto-tune.
Indra: running experiments now, will post EOD summary with numbers and a minimal repro + commands. deploy-bot: queueing kv-repro job on infra-qa.
deploy-bot: job/kv-repro-1930001122 queued -> running.
Indra: :eyes:
